expansion_xu_lin_close_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_close_001.text: Lin wiped the slate, then retained one line at the top: One person at a time. Yue asked whether she could carry that instruction into future meetings. Lin looked amused and wrote, You can remember it without carrying me everywhere. The answer caught Yue's habit of turning an encounter into a portable symbol. This woman had work, a rest interval, and opinions Yue had not earned the right to organize. Yue put away her notebook before she could make the moment more elegant than it was.

expansion_xu_lin_close_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_close_002.text: Bao lifted the carpenter's square again. Lin returned toward the ordinary indicators, choosing the drier boards along the landing without waiting for either of them. Yue watched only until the mechanic reached her own tool chest. The hollow beneath the seal remained the defect Bao had shown her. The bracket remained a separate question. Neither the insult from the boatman nor Yue's wish to defend Lin could supply the missing crew, change the allowance, or close the timber gap.

expansion_xu_lin_support_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_support_001.text: Yue drew the two supports on her own page before touching the bowl. Lin checked the drawing and pushed it back: the second support was too high. Yue corrected it. Then Lin let her hold the rod against each resting place while the water stayed still. A change in support altered the apparent mark without altering the bowl's contents. Yue had expected a proof that Lin's scratch was correct. She had instead learned why agreement with a scratch was insufficient.

expansion_xu_lin_support_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_support_002.text: Bao asked whether she could now tell the gate crew which mark to use. Yue said no. The bowl showed one possible error, while the actual instrument still needed its ordinary check at its own mounting. She could identify the question to ask without borrowing the authority to answer it. Lin gave a short nod and reclaimed the rod. The comparison had consumed most of the interval. Yue would have to leave the estimate's treatment of the bracket for Bao's scheduled discussion.

expansion_xu_lin_support_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_support_003.text: She recorded the demonstration as a changed-support comparison in a still bowl. She did not write that the canal's level had been proved, or that the old bracket explained every disputed reading. Lin watched the sentence being written and added a small arrow beside the word bowl. Yue left the arrow there. Her notebook was becoming less graceful as other people's precise objections entered it. She could accept that price more readily than the price of a handsome page that preserved her first mistake.

expansion_xu_lin_record_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_record_001.text: Yue held her notebook open but kept the pencil still. Lin wrote, My explanation, yes. My old customers, no. A list of initials occupied the rod's back, and Yue realized she had already memorized two of them. She drew the mounting without the names. When Lin corrected its angle, Yue rewrote the whole sentence instead of putting the correction in a tiny margin. If the record was supposed to serve them both, legibility could not remain a courtesy reserved for its owner.

expansion_xu_lin_record_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_record_002.text: Bao began to summarize the mechanics aloud. Yue stopped him long enough to put the summary where Lin could see it. The pause embarrassed him, then relieved him. Lin crossed out his description of the scratch as a new standard. It was a working reference from an earlier mounting check. Yue had nearly copied his convenient phrase. Hearing a fluent explanation had made the meaning feel settled before the person who owned it could object.

expansion_xu_lin_record_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_record_003.text: They used the remaining interval to agree on the narrow note Yue could retain. The mounting needed comparison during the equipment's regular check; their conversation had made no new level determination. Yue had no time left to test the bowl herself. That absence belonged in the record too. Lin took her slate back, leaving Yue with a page that documented a question and the limits of its explanation. It was useful, though less impressive than the discovery she had hoped to make.

expansion_xu_lin_estimate_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_estimate_001.text: Yue asked Bao whether the bracket was included with the seal repair. He said the existing allowance covered the ordered timber, seals, and nails; he would need to check the small fittings before naming any additional work. Lin read Yue's written question and placed one fingertip against the bracket. She had found wear, not issued a purchase order. Yue had been ready to treat a technical observation as though it carried its own funding. The distinction made the job harder to imagine and easier to describe.

expansion_xu_lin_estimate_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_estimate_002.text: Bao drew a line between the material gap under the seal and the uncertain mounting. Fixing one did not guarantee the other would read correctly. Yue asked him to retain that distinction when the crew was confirmed. He agreed to include it in the ordinary discussion, without promising an additional repair or a quicker completion. Lin tapped the slate: Don't use my name to make the allowance larger. Yue copied the instruction into her own notes and let Lin see it.

expansion_xu_lin_estimate_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_estimate_003.text: By then the bowl demonstration had been put away. Yue had missed an opportunity to understand the instrument directly. She could feel herself wanting to compensate with a stronger sentence about the estimate. Instead she wrote that the fitting question remained open. Bao thanked her for separating it from the visible leak. Lin gave no thanks; she was already tying the rod to her belt. The mechanic's next obligation did not include rewarding Yue for having learned where her authority ended.

expansion_xu_lin_choice.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_choice.text: Lin waited with her hand on the measuring rod. Yue had one short interval to use well. Which uncertainty should she address first?

choices.text: Compare the support positions and distinguish the apparent reading change.
Ask what may be recorded, and make the explanation readable to both of them.
Leave the gauge untouched and ask Bao where bracket work belongs in the existing estimate.

expansion_xu_lin_common_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_common_001.text: Someone tapped twice on the square with a wooden pencil. Bao turned and stepped aside. The woman behind him wore her tools on a broad cloth belt, each handle tied through its own loop. A slate hung against her hip. She looked at Yue's mouth, then at the timber, and raised a palm before either of them could speak. Bao waited until she had set down a narrow measuring rod. He introduced her as Xu Lin, the mechanic who maintained the landing's ordinary indicators.

expansion_xu_lin_common_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_common_002.text: Lin pointed to her ear, shook her head, and held the slate toward Yue. On it she had written, Face me. One person at a time. Yue stopped arranging her explanation while Bao was still giving his. She had mistaken the mechanic's stillness for permission to fill it. Lin watched her notice the mistake, then wiped a small space clean with her sleeve. The gesture offered room for a conversation. It did not ask Yue to demonstrate how considerate she could be.

expansion_xu_lin_common_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_common_003.text: Yue wrote her name. Lin read it, wrote her own beside it, and underlined the second character. Bao made a motion as though to explain its meaning. Lin caught his sleeve and pointed back at the seal. He smiled with the embarrassment of a familiar correction. Names could wait for leisure; the work allowance could not. Yue liked the woman immediately, which was another reason to be careful. Affection had sometimes encouraged her to believe a person before she understood what the person had actually claimed.

expansion_xu_lin_common_004.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_common_004.text: The rod had three marks cut across its pale face. Beside the lowest, a shorter line had been scratched rather than carved. Yue compared both with the wet streak on the gate shoe. The scratched line seemed to agree with the water. She wanted that agreement to mean she had found the trustworthy mark. Lin turned the rod over. A date and two initials occupied the back. The front looked like an instrument; the back reminded Yue that someone had made it under particular conditions.

expansion_xu_lin_common_005.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_common_005.text: Lin drew a basin, a gate, and a stick resting against the basin's rim. Beneath the stick she drew two different supports. Bao supplied a spoken sentence only after Lin nodded: the old support had worn lower, so a reading taken there could resemble a change in water level. Lin tapped the drawing of the support. Then she tapped the actual bracket. The instruction was exact enough for Yue to understand without guessing at a lost word. A shared diagram had become part of their conversation.

expansion_xu_lin_common_006.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_common_006.text: Across the landing, a boatman called that a hired mechanic would always find a reason to hire herself again. Bao glanced toward him. Lin saw the movement and asked what had been said. Yue could have softened it into a question about maintenance. Instead she wrote the sentence as closely as she remembered it. Lin read without smiling. She added, Sometimes a repair is unnecessary. Sometimes a man wants an unnecessary repair to be the only kind I am allowed to find.

expansion_xu_lin_common_007.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_common_007.text: She took the rod back. Its marks were hers to explain, and the insult had not made them public property. Yue felt the small sting of losing an object she had begun to treat as evidence in her own inquiry. Lin was here to maintain equipment, not to provide a stranger with a satisfying lesson. Bao checked the sun's position above the storehouse. They had time for a brief comparison before he needed to return to the ordinary repair sequence. They did not have time to settle the boatman's prejudice.

expansion_xu_lin_common_008.speaker: narrator
expansion_xu_lin_common_008.text: Lin placed an empty bowl beneath the bracket and poured a little water into it from her own flask. The bowl was a demonstration, not a substitute for a reading in the canal. Yue could compare a changed support, ask Lin which observations belonged in her notebook, or leave the instrument alone and examine how the repair estimate treated the bracket. Each would answer a different question. If she tried all three, Bao would lose the interval he had offered, and Lin would lose the rest she had planned.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_close_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_close_001.text: The otter slid into a shallow channel beyond the working shoe, its long tail briefly visible between the roots. Yue made no announcement about its intentions. The closed hand gate had given them a bounded interval, not custody of everything that happened beside it. Luo turned back to the waiting crew. The child brought the whistle out from behind his back and wiped its mouthpiece on his sleeve.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_close_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_close_002.text: Yue looked once more at the split wood. The object could support an account of damage and retrieval. It could not tell her whether the child would remember the splash differently tomorrow, or whether the grandfather's fear of a delayed boat would find another explanation. The otter had left them no testimony. They still had the actual obstruction they had removed, the observed lock movement, and a wet little whistle whose owner was about to try it again.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_observe_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_observe_001.text: Yue counted the animal's visible actions instead of naming its purpose. It rubbed one paw across the stone, lifted it, and turned toward a patch of shallower light. When a rope knocked against a boat rail, it paused. Yue could not tell whether the noise had startled it, whether it was listening for something else, or whether the pause had no connection with the boat. She wrote the sequence without arranging it into a message. The order was information; the motive remained a guess.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_observe_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_observe_002.text: The child said the otter had looked guilty. Yue asked what a guilty otter would do differently from a wary one. He frowned, then suggested it would hide. At that moment the animal slipped behind the root. He pointed triumphantly. Yue did not argue that hiding proved innocence. She asked him whether an otter with no whistle to hide might also prefer the root. The question spoiled his neat proof. It did not spoil the creature, which reappeared carrying the same pebble.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_observe_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_observe_003.text: Watching consumed the interval. Yue had not examined the child's memory in detail or learned the crew's reporting procedure. She closed her notebook with a small, unsatisfying result: an animal had handled a stone beside a lock, and no visible action explained the whistle beneath the gate shoe. The child looked disappointed. Yue let the disappointment stand. If every careful observation had to end in an exciting conclusion, she would eventually begin supplying one.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_memory_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_memory_001.text: Yue crouched on the dry boards so the child would not have to speak upward. She asked where he had last held the whistle before it went missing. He said he had leaned over to see the boat scrape along the lock wall. Then he said he had heard a splash. He could not remember whether the whistle was still in his hand at that moment. Yue repeated those details and asked whether she had changed any of them. He corrected her: the boat had scraped before he leaned.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_memory_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_memory_002.text: The correction mattered more than his first confident claim about the beast. Yue told him they could retain the sequence without deciding exactly how the whistle had fallen. He asked whether that meant she thought he was careless. She said a missing detail was not a verdict about his character. The word verdict was too large; she tried again. They knew where the whistle had stopped. They did not know everything about its journey. He studied the split mouthpiece instead of looking at the otter.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_memory_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_memory_003.text: By the time he finished, the creature had moved behind the roots. Yue could not add its departure to any observation of her own. The child asked if he could still tell his grandfather that he had seen an otter. She said yes. He could describe the pebble too. A truthful encounter did not need to carry the lost whistle in its mouth. He seemed almost persuaded, though Yue suspected he would improve the story later. She could offer a distinction; she could not supervise every retelling.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_procedure_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_procedure_001.text: Luo said a person who saw something caught at the gate should point out the location from the bank and tell the working crew. They should not reach into the moving apparatus to establish a better story. The whistle's retrieval had required the hand gate to be closed and the ordinary indicator to settle. Yue asked whether a creature near the bank should be reported in the same way. Luo said proximity alone was no obstruction. The report should describe the condition that affected the gate.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_procedure_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_procedure_002.text: Yue gave the child an example: something pale beneath the shoe, or a branch lodged where the gate should travel. The child supplied another: a monster looking wicked. Luo shook her head. A look could not tell her where to place a pole or whether to stop a boat. Yue almost laughed, then saw the child's tightened mouth. He was trying to join a grown conversation with the language he had. She asked him to point to the place a worker would need to inspect instead.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_procedure_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_procedure_003.text: He pointed to the gate shoe. That was enough for this lesson. Yue had not watched the otter closely, and its pebble remained outside her account. Luo returned to the lock's ordinary sequence, satisfied that no one had been sent onto the root bank. The child kept the whistle behind his back a little longer. Yue understood why instructions about reporting had not relieved his fear of blame. A useful procedure could make the next response safer without making today's embarrassment disappear.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_choice.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_choice.text: The otter set its pebble down and looked toward the water. Yue kept her feet on the boards. What should she do with the uncertainty?

choices.text: Watch quietly from the landing and record only visible behaviour.
Ask the child to separate what he saw from what he imagined.
Ask Luo how a real future obstruction should be reported without blaming an animal.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_common_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_common_001.text: The child followed Yue's glance toward a narrow strip of bank above the lock. Something brown and green moved among the exposed roots. A tidemirror otter had climbed onto a stone, carrying a pebble against its breast. The pearly patches along its shoulders caught the light. The child drew the broken whistle behind his back. Yue remained on the dry boards. The upstream hand gate was still closed; neither curiosity nor the successful retrieval had made the water a place for an unscheduled approach.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_common_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_common_002.text: The otter rolled the pebble between its paws. Once it dropped the stone and caught it against a root. The child whispered that the creature was showing how it had swallowed his whistle. Yue looked at the split mouthpiece in his hand. They had just lifted that mouthpiece from beneath the gate shoe. A stone held on the bank could not change where the whistle had been found. Yet the child's explanation gathered force from the animal's beauty, as though an unusual shoulder pattern made an ordinary gesture more informative.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_common_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_common_003.text: Luo signaled to a waiting boatman that the interval before reopening remained hers to manage. Yue asked whether the root bank was part of the lock crew's inspection ground. Luo said no: they watched for obstructions at the working gate, not every creature that occupied the adjoining bank. Her answer limited the encounter. Yue could not turn the otter into a suspect to justify reaching beyond the crew's task, or declare the bank harmless because a child wanted a friendly animal.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_common_004.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_common_004.text: The child wanted his whistle to have belonged to an adventure. A swallowed whistle sounded better than a dropped one. Yue understood the appetite too easily. In her first months at the sect, she had preferred a mysterious impediment to a badly placed thumb. She had not lied each time. Sometimes she had simply looked longer at the explanation she wanted, until its alternatives seemed dull enough to forget. The otter sniffed its pebble. Its indifference offered no correction they could quote.

expansion_tidemirror_otter_common_005.speaker: narrator
expansion_tidemirror_otter_common_005.text: The grandfather was approaching along the bank, still occupied with the delayed boat. The child asked Yue to tell him what the creature had meant. She had a little time before the ordinary lock operation resumed. She could watch without approaching, help the child distinguish what he remembered from what they had found, or ask Luo how to report an actual future obstruction. None of those would make the animal explain itself. The choice was about their next human claim.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_close_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_close_001.text: The pangolin stopped digging and pressed its nose into the seam. Yue could not see what it found. Shi Lan released the brake only after the space beside the wheel was clear, and the cart rolled on without driving the animal from the shelter. The girl looked back until the turn hid its scales. The wet kindling remained beneath the damaged roof. Their pause had produced a bounded account, not a complete repair of the roadside.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_close_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_close_002.text: Yue slid the sketch into its cloth cover. The cart's movement unsettled her pencil marks, making them seem as slight as they were. She had wanted the creature, the girl's fear, and the broken tiles to form a single comprehensible problem. The afternoon offered no such agreement. Shi Lan moved the quilt away from the brake lever again, preparing to tell her why a warden could care about a waiting roof and still continue toward a different obligation.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_ground_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_ground_001.text: Yue traced the little runoff channel with her eyes from the road's edge to the seam. She did not step onto the loose patch to see whether it would support her. Water had reached the sheltered soil from above, and the animal was digging where the damp earth separated easily. Those facts could coexist without either explaining the other. She told Shi Lan the seam looked recently disturbed. The warden asked which part of that phrase came from sight and which from an estimate of time.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_ground_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_ground_002.text: Yue withdrew recently. She could describe pale exposed soil and a darker wet rim. She had not watched the place before the pangolin arrived. The correction annoyed her because it made her report sound less expert. Shi Lan said it made the report easier to check. A later traveler could compare the same seam; no one could inspect Yue's private sense of how fresh it seemed. The animal stretched one claw under a root, indifferent to the improvement in their vocabulary.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_ground_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_ground_003.text: The driver's bell sounded again. Yue had used their interval without hearing the girl's full story. She recorded the roadside position on her own sketch and added that she had made no slope inspection. The phrase felt unnecessarily defensive until she imagined it detached from the rest of the page. A quarry owner could quote a sect traveler's observation for purposes she had never intended. She owed the future reader a boundary that would remain visible even if her confidence traveled farther than her actual view.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_story_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_story_001.text: Yue asked what the girl's aunt had actually seen. A pangolin crossing a track, the girl said, after the quarry workers had come down for supper. The collapse had happened the next morning. She did not know whether rain had fallen overnight, whether the face had been worked that day, or whether anyone else had seen the animal. Yue repeated the two events without adding a connecting verb. The girl looked dissatisfied, then said the aunt had been frightened even before the collapse.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_story_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_story_002.text: That fear was part of the account. Yue wrote it beside the sighting instead of treating it as knowledge of the coming failure. The driver said his own fright before a bad delivery never counted as wisdom. His tone had softened, though the comparison still belonged to him. The girl asked whether Yue would laugh at her aunt. Yue said no. She could respect the woman's fear and leave the claimed warning unproved. The answer lacked the triumph of defending every sentence on the girl's behalf.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_story_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_story_003.text: They did not learn anything more about the soil beneath this shrine. Yue closed the sketch without inventing a local explanation for the quarry story. The girl thanked her for hearing it and immediately asked whether pangolins could foresee rain. Yue said she did not know. She resisted turning ignorance into a promise to investigate. The cart's journey already had work attached to it, and listening to a person did not authorize Yue to spend someone else's afternoon proving the person's hopes.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_roof_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_roof_001.text: Yue drew the shrine's turn beside two recognizable trees and marked the three missing tiles. She described the wet sticks as wet sticks. The pangolin did not appear in the repair request. If the receiving village needed to know why kindling failed to stay dry, the absent roof pieces were already a condition someone could inspect. A striking animal could make a note memorable while also drawing attention away from the ordinary defect that required work.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_roof_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_roof_002.text: Shi Lan asked whether Yue had promised to mend the shrine. She had not. Had she named a crew or offered payment? Neither. Yue added that the note requested inspection when village work could be arranged. The phrase felt cold beside the soaked little woodpile. She wanted to erase it and write something that sounded caring. Shi Lan did not let her borrow concern as a purchase order. Yue retained the sentence and made the location drawing clearer instead.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_roof_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_roof_003.text: The following driver accepted a copy to carry onward only after confirming that his ordinary route passed the receiving village. He promised delivery of the note, not a repaired roof. Yue thanked him for that specific task. She had spent the pause on the shelter and learned little about the pangolin. The choice left her curious. It also left the driver with a small, defined obligation he had chosen, rather than a picturesque story that expected him to infer what generosity should mean.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_choice.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_choice.text: The pangolin scraped once more beneath the sill. Yue had a brief roadside pause, no quarry access, and no reason to touch the animal. Where should her attention go?

choices.text: Compare the visible runoff and disturbed soil without extending the observation to a quarry.
Hear the girl's recollection and distinguish remembered sequence from a prediction.
Write the receiving village a specific roof repair note while the animal stays undisturbed.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_001.text: A low scrape came from beneath the shrine's raised sill. Shi Lan stopped the cart on the firm part of the road and set the brake before looking. A cinderback pangolin was working its foreclaws into a seam of loose earth. Slate and terracotta scales shifted across its shoulders. Yue had seen drawings that made the mineral edges blaze like a furnace. Here they held the flat light of a damp afternoon. The animal's actual size made the storybook fires seem especially extravagant.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_002.text: The driver behind them rang a small bell. Shi Lan raised two fingers to ask for a moment, then moved aside so the road remained visible. She was watching the animal's distance from the cart, not declaring the damaged shrine closed to everyone. Yue stayed beside the wheel. The wet kindling lay above the pangolin's back, screened by a broken board. Its claws made a noise like a person worrying a stubborn drawer. The resemblance tempted her to imagine frustration where she could observe only repeated movement.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_003.text: The following driver said creatures with hot scales should be useful for drying the shrine wood. Shi Lan asked whether he had ever seen one dry anything. He laughed and said it was a joke. Yue laughed too late. She had been considering how near the creature would need to stand. The warden noticed. She did not correct Yue aloud; she simply pointed to the rain-dark sticks and then to the empty space between them and the animal. Nothing in that space carried the heat Yue had supplied.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_004.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_004.text: A girl riding beside the driver said her aunt had found a pangolin near a quarry face the day before a collapse. The driver told her not to trouble a sect traveler with nursery fears. Yue disliked his dismissal. She also disliked the possibility that her dislike would make the story seem stronger. A creature might occupy disturbed ground for many ordinary reasons. One remembered sighting and one later collapse did not establish a warning system, however unkindly the first person had been silenced.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_005.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_005.text: The pangolin curled its tail away from a dripping corner. Its feet remained on the loose ground beneath the shelter. Yue could see a shallow channel where rain had run off the road. That observation belonged to this roadside seam, not to the quarry in the girl's account. Shi Lan checked the brake again. They could spend a few minutes here without missing the cart's next ordinary stop, but she would not turn a roadside pause into an expedition up an uninspected slope.

expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_006.speaker: narrator
expansion_cinderback_pangolin_common_006.text: The choice troubled Yue because each useful question left another unanswered. She could inspect the visible ground from the road and keep its scale exact. She could listen to the girl's recollection without adopting its omen. Or she could use the pause to write the shelter repair note, allowing the creature to remain an animal with its own occupied patch of earth. The roof would still need tiles. The cart would still need to move. Attention could choose its object without making everything else cease to matter.

expansion_chen_rui_close_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_close_001.text: Chen left by the public path, carrying the paper he had used and no copy of Fen's ticket. The glossary remained on its proper shelf. Yue knew a little more about the choices in front of them, but the missing contract had not arrived while they spoke. No advocate's manner could fill its recipient space. He Ming waited for Fen to decide how much of the search she wanted recorded.

expansion_chen_rui_close_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_close_002.text: Fen unfolded the ticket again. The crease crossed an old ink stroke, making the name look briefly different under the light. Yue did not offer to flatten it or keep it safe. Its owner could hold it imperfectly and still own it. The question about the spelling discrepancy remained available. So did the cost of another morning at the landing, which none of the brief explanations had paid.

expansion_chen_rui_example_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_example_001.text: Yue proposed a fictional carrier who retained a receipt but lacked the agreement setting its payment conditions. Chen asked whether the carrier wanted a copy of the agreement or payment under it. Yue said both. He drew two separate lines on a scrap he owned. The first asked where the agreement could be found. The second asserted a payment right that they had not established. Combining them would make a clerk answer the claim, perhaps without addressing the missing copy.

expansion_chen_rui_example_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_example_002.text: Yue changed the fictional carrier into a worker's relative. Chen said the substitution introduced another unresolved question: what entitled that person to receive the document or money? He did not claim that relatives had no rights. He refused to invent the relevant authority from their affection. Fen listened with her mouth pressed tight. Yue kept the example fictional and did not supply the names or wording on the folded ticket. The distinction helped her and cost the girl patience.

expansion_chen_rui_example_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_example_003.text: He Ming said the public office could record an information request within its own work. Yue thanked Chen without commissioning a letter. The scrap remained his; she copied only the general distinction into her notebook. She had learned a way to frame a question, not a ruling on Fen's claim. When she turned back, Fen was staring toward the water. Yue had spent the interval improving a request while the person she meant to help endured another conversation about the limits of help.

expansion_chen_rui_office_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_office_001.text: Yue asked He Ming which question the office could address today without pretending to possess the voyage contract. He said it could record a spelling discrepancy if Fen wanted that recorded, and direct an inquiry about the missing agreement through the ordinary channel. Neither act would name a recipient in a blank space. Chen nodded but added no authority to the answer. Yue left the advocate's offered explanation where it belonged: an available service, not an instruction binding the public office.

expansion_chen_rui_office_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_office_002.text: Chen said an office request and a private letter could duplicate each other. Yue asked whether duplication always harmed a search. He said no, but contradictory wording could make the two look like different claims. He had seen that happen elsewhere; he had not reviewed this case. Yue wrote the warning as a general risk and refused the tempting phrase the advocate confirms. He had confirmed nothing about the ticket. He Ming's narrow answer was still the only office action named in their exchange.

expansion_chen_rui_office_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_office_003.text: The interval ended before Yue tested the reasoning with an example. Chen took his scrap paper back and checked that the glossary had reached its shelf. Fen retained the ticket. Yue could not tell whether the girl had heard the distinctions or simply waited for the grown voices to stop. She asked He Ming to address the next question to Fen herself. Organizing a request could become another way of taking a person's search away from her if Yue kept answering on her behalf.

expansion_chen_rui_pause_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_pause_001.text: Yue thanked Chen for stating the limits of his offer and said they would not use the interval for a consultation. He accepted the answer without leaving a paper in Fen's hand. That ordinary courtesy made the refusal easier to maintain. Yue had feared she would need to prove the advice unwanted before she could decline it. Fen looked from one adult to the other, surprised that a conversation offered for free could end without an explanation of how grateful she ought to be.

expansion_chen_rui_pause_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_pause_002.text: Chen returned to the glossary shelf. Yue asked Fen whether she wanted a little silence or to return directly to He Ming's question. Fen said she wanted people to stop saying that they understood. Yue had been about to say exactly that. She closed her mouth. The silence did not make the girl's fear easier to bear; it removed one demand to translate the fear into something a helper could recognize and answer.

expansion_chen_rui_pause_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_pause_003.text: They stayed beside the public board until He Ming signaled that he could continue. Yue had learned nothing more about letter wording. That uncertainty remained real, and she would need to address it if the office required a written request later. For now she let Fen keep the paper and the next answer. She had not rescued the girl from the rent she was losing or the father she could not find. She had merely stopped using every available minute as proof of her own usefulness.

expansion_chen_rui_choice.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_choice.text: Fen kept the folded ticket in her hand. Yue would not give it to the advocate. What, if anything, should she ask before returning to the office's next step?

choices.text: Test the difference between locating a contract and claiming payment with an invented example.
Ask He Ming to identify the office's next step, and keep the advocate's offer separate.
End the consultation and give Fen the choice of when to hear more.

expansion_chen_rui_common_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_common_001.text: A man in a russet sash waited beside the public writing board, outside the hiring-office threshold. He had been watching the queue rather than the ticket. When Yue looked toward him, he turned his palms outward to show he carried no office seal. He introduced himself as Chen Rui, a contract advocate whose workroom faced the fish market. He had come to return a borrowed glossary. His title gave him no claim on Fen's paper, and he made no attempt to cross the threshold.

expansion_chen_rui_common_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_common_002.text: Fen folded the ticket until only its blank back showed. Chen noticed and addressed Yue instead. If she was considering an inquiry, he could explain how he distinguished a request to locate an agreement from a demand to pay a claim. He did not need the child's document for that explanation. Yue felt relieved by the careful offer. Relief was dangerous here: a useful stranger might become an authority in her mind before anyone had checked what work he was qualified or authorized to perform.

expansion_chen_rui_common_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_common_003.text: Chen put the returned glossary on the public board and asked He Ming where its owner wanted it. He Ming pointed to a dry shelf. Their brief exchange established a mundane reason for Chen's presence. It proved neither his reliability as an advocate nor any connection with the missing voyage contract. Yue had become practiced at mistrusting grand entrances. She was less practiced at recognizing how an ordinary, considerate action could persuade her to fill in everything she had not yet learned.

expansion_chen_rui_common_004.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_common_004.text: Chen said his usual clients were small carriers and warehouse tenants. He charged for reading documents and drafting letters. A brief general explanation here would cost nothing, but it would not create a client agreement. Fen glanced up at the mention of charges. Chen met her eyes long enough to say that he would not request money from her in this queue. Then he looked back to Yue, leaving Fen room to decide whether she wished to hear anything.

expansion_chen_rui_common_005.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_common_005.text: Yue asked why he had offered the explanation. He said people often arrived at his workroom angry with a letter that had requested the wrong thing. Some had paid another writer first. Their disappointment could become his business, which was not a pure reason to care about the problem. Yue appreciated the admission and distrusted her appreciation. A disclosed interest was still an interest. She could use the explanation without converting candour into a guarantee that his advice fitted this particular paper.

expansion_chen_rui_common_006.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_common_006.text: Fen said she wanted her father back, not a lesson about letters. Chen answered that a letter could ask for information without pretending to bring anyone home. Yue heard how inadequate the sentence sounded. She also heard the promise he had declined to make. The queue shifted a little, and He Ming glanced toward the waiting people. There was time for one short exchange before they needed to return to the ordinary work already before them.

expansion_chen_rui_common_007.speaker: narrator
expansion_chen_rui_common_007.text: Yue could ask Chen to demonstrate the distinction using an invented example. She could compare the public office's next step with the limited task he had offered, without opening Fen's paper again. Or she could end the conversation and let Fen retain her attention. Asking for more would have a price even while it was free: the girl's waiting time, He Ming's divided attention, and the chance that an articulate stranger's categories would begin to displace the family whose search they were meant to serve.

expansion_wu_zheng_close_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_close_001.text: Wu carried the shuttle toward the public passage, the strap tucked into its own bag. He had told them where his observations came from and retained the right to be absent from the next day's test. Yue watched the space beside the bell become empty. An interesting visitor could make a hall feel wiser without changing a single operating condition. She had to distinguish that feeling from the work still to be done.

expansion_wu_zheng_close_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_close_002.text: Luo checked that the tour could continue. The ordinary fan remained unpowered, and no one had rung the bell beside it under a running condition. Yue kept those facts near the top of her notes. The next demonstration would concern the supplementary array's empty fuel cage. She would count what was actually available there, carrying neither a loom master's analogy nor her desire for a complete lesson into the missing holder.

expansion_wu_zheng_signal_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_signal_001.text: Wu allowed Yue to touch the loose end of the strap. It was unconnected to any powered equipment. He asked her to look away while he moved it, then asked what she had noticed. A tug, she said. He had also lifted it slightly; she had missed that movement. The exercise showed a limit in her description of this particular demonstration. It did not show what a fan would mask, or how a worker would recognize a danger signal in the kiln.

expansion_wu_zheng_signal_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_signal_002.text: Yue asked whether training made an unnoticed motion safe. Wu said training could give a person expectations and practiced actions; it could not make an unperformed check happen. Luo added that tomorrow's ordinary test had to use its specified location and condition. The two answers resisted being combined into a pleasing assurance. Yue had wanted experienced workers to solve the problem merely by being experienced. Their experience had instead helped them state what experience could not guarantee.

expansion_wu_zheng_signal_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_signal_003.text: She wrote a question for the crew's own consideration: whether the test should distinguish a sound being present from a worker identifying the signal. Luo accepted it as a question, not as an added procedure they had agreed to perform. Wu took back the strap. Yue had used the interval on comprehension and left its reporting language to Luo. The distinction would be easier to preserve in the work than in a story about the clever visitor who had fixed the alarm.

expansion_wu_zheng_attribution_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_attribution_001.text: Yue read aloud the sentence she wanted to write, facing Wu so he could stop her. He removed the words proves that. He also removed the description of him as the kiln's safety adviser. She had not meant to invent a position; the title had seemed a courteous shorthand for a useful question. Wu said courtesy was a poor reason to put responsibility on a stranger. He repaired shuttles. He had come here with one and expected to leave with it.

expansion_wu_zheng_attribution_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_attribution_002.text: She rewrote the note as a visitor's analogy from loom work, offered without a finding about the fan. Luo asked to see the finished sentence before it entered the tour's account. Yue understood his interest. A later reader could mistake the quiet demonstration for the missing running-condition check if the notes made the visit sound complete. Wu agreed that Yue could retain the comment under those limits. He did not agree to attend tomorrow or to endorse whatever answer the crew obtained.

expansion_wu_zheng_attribution_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_attribution_003.text: The remaining time was too short for the strap exercise. Yue had preserved the scope of the comment without testing the comparison herself. Her notebook held a duller sentence than the one she had first proposed. Wu seemed content with that. He slipped the shuttle into a cloth sleeve, ready to continue his own errand when the tour moved on. Yue let him leave the note less memorable and his obligations no larger.

expansion_wu_zheng_tools_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_tools_001.text: Yue asked whether the strap should be moved within his reach or remain flat for inspection. Wu said flat, please. The edge he needed to examine curled when it was folded. He pointed to a different space where the shuttle sleeve could go. Yue moved only the sleeve. Her first helpful arrangement would have interrupted the work he was doing while he waited. The correction was so ordinary that she felt foolish for having made the question into a trial of her kindness.

expansion_wu_zheng_tools_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_tools_002.text: Luo lifted the loose stool rather than ask Wu to shift his braced leg. Wu thanked him and said the stool's new position still blocked the path he planned to take. Luo moved it again. No one had solved the layout by observing a disability from across the room. They had asked the person who would use the route. Yue collected an empty cup only after checking that it was finished with. The hall became a little easier to leave, without anyone announcing an example of good conduct.

expansion_wu_zheng_tools_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_tools_003.text: They had spent the interval on the actual bench. Yue learned no more about signal recognition and added no analogy to the tour report. Wu put his crutch under his left arm, gripped it securely, and kept the sleeved shuttle in his right hand. He would choose his own pace. Yue remained beside Luo instead of hovering behind the visitor. A modest piece of work had been completed, and the alarm question remained exactly as untested as before.

expansion_wu_zheng_choice.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_choice.text: The bell had fallen silent. Wu's comparison could improve a question without proving tomorrow's result. Yue had time for one short exchange before Luo continued the tour.

choices.text: Distinguish knowing a signal from perceiving it, using an empty strap demonstration.
Ask permission to record Wu's comment as a bounded analogy rather than a test finding.
Ask Wu how he wants his tools placed before clearing the bench for the next visitors.

expansion_wu_zheng_common_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_common_001.text: A visitor sitting beyond the bell beam lifted an ordinary wooden shuttle. Yue had thought he was waiting for Luo. He had been waiting for the sound to end. He introduced himself as Wu Zheng, a retired loom master who still repaired small weaving tools for former apprentices. His left knee rested in a fitted brace. A crutch stood within his left hand's reach, and a folded strap lay across the bench beside him. Nothing about the arrangement invited Yue to test how much assistance he might accept.

expansion_wu_zheng_common_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_common_002.text: Wu asked Luo whether tomorrow's fan check would use the actual working signal or merely the bell demonstrated to applicants. Luo said the purpose was to learn what could be heard at the required location under the stated running condition. He had not answered it today. Wu nodded, then turned the shuttle over in his right hand. He had brought a strap for a worker who wanted a loom repaired after the kiln visit. His own errand was not a request to join the heated-air trial.

expansion_wu_zheng_common_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_common_003.text: The old man said a loom master's signal could reach an apprentice who already expected it and fail to reach a new worker standing in the same place. Yue asked if he meant the new worker had poorer hearing. Wu said expectation could change which noise a person attended to. He could recall examples from his former room; he had no measurements for this hall. Yue almost wrote a general law. He tapped the notebook with the shuttle's blunt end before she could.

expansion_wu_zheng_common_004.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_common_004.text: The strap was worn along one edge. Wu laid it flat on the bench and pointed to the original fold. A familiar hand would find the pull without looking, he said. A visiting hand might choose another part of the same material. Neither observation certified a kiln alarm. He enjoyed the analogy, but he was unwilling to let enjoyment carry it into a test report. Yue found that harder than simply detecting a false claim. An interesting comparison could be useful precisely where it stopped being evidence.

expansion_wu_zheng_common_005.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_common_005.text: Luo needed to finish the cold visit before the ordinary hall work resumed. He offered Wu time to state one concern for tomorrow's check. Wu refused to become its author just because he had mentioned a loom. The crew who performed the fan check would decide its procedure within their existing task. Yue could ask about the difference between a signal and a practiced response, make sure the visitor's comment was attributed within its limits, or help clear the bench after asking which objects should remain where they were.

expansion_wu_zheng_common_006.speaker: narrator
expansion_wu_zheng_common_006.text: She noticed that the folded strap lay just beyond Wu's easy reach. She also noticed herself constructing a benevolent scene in which she moved it closer before he asked. The strap's position might be inconvenient. It might be deliberate. He was holding the shuttle in his right hand and had placed the crutch where he wanted it. Yue could ask. The opportunity did not become urgent simply because she had noticed his brace.

expansion_song_mei_close_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_close_001.text: Song wrapped the drum's patched rim in a soft cloth and set it beside her bag. She had an evening's paid work ahead and no commission from Yue. The driver took his empty bowl to the cook, careful now to compliment the beans within her hearing. Yue stood when Tuo came for her. Her lunch had become a conversation with several people whose lives would continue after she left the shade.

expansion_song_mei_close_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_close_002.text: The memory of the kiln's damp firewood remained her own imperfect contribution. She could tell it again without claiming that the sky had acquired a debt or that a performer had certified a desert road. Across the yard, jars waited near the cistern steps. Yue followed Tuo toward the ordinary lifting, measuring, and payment that a song could make poignant but could not perform.

expansion_song_mei_rhythm_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_rhythm_001.text: Song sang one short line at two different speeds, using the same words. Yue felt the slower version give the traveler more room to hesitate. The hesitation belonged to the telling; it did not add a mile to the remembered road. She said so, and Song asked whether a listener who had never walked there would know which pauses were expressive. Yue answered that the listener might not. A confidence in her own ear could not become a guarantee for everyone else's inference.

expansion_song_mei_rhythm_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_rhythm_002.text: The performer tapped the patched edge once. A damaged instrument could influence the arrangement too. Yue wanted to classify the sources of every sound: breath, drama, repair, remembered distance. Song said some overlapped, and she could not always reconstruct the first reason for a choice she had kept for years. Yue wrote that uncertainty beside the short example. She did not turn the two performances into a rule for decoding old songs.

expansion_song_mei_rhythm_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_rhythm_003.text: They had used the interval on timing and learned no new well condition. Song kept the line within the table's hearing rather than sing a full verse for the yard. Yue thanked her for the limited demonstration. It was an odd pleasure to enjoy a beautiful phrase after removing the information she had hoped it carried. The song could remain useful as a song. Her thirst would need a different kind of answer.

expansion_song_mei_memory_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_memory_001.text: Song described a verse about a cart wheel that broke beside a pale ridge. She had inherited the verse from a singer who was already old when they met. Song had seen a broken wheel on a different journey and used its sound when she performed the older account. The two experiences met in the song. They did not become one witnessed event. Yue asked whether she could write that distinction down. Song agreed to the explanation but did not grant permission to copy the entire verse.

expansion_song_mei_memory_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_memory_002.text: Yue recorded the sources without requesting the old singer's private story. Song said an audience sometimes trusted a line more when she named the dead person behind it. That trust might be deserved, or it might be an effect of a name no listener could question. She disliked being rewarded for making an account harder to challenge. Yue heard a professional concern she had not expected from the joke at the next table. The singer's craft contained its own temptations to sound certain.

expansion_song_mei_memory_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_memory_003.text: The explanation took the remaining interval. Yue had not heard the rhythm comparison and could not claim to distinguish route days from musical pauses by ear. She closed the notebook before Song needed to ask twice. The inherited verse remained unwritten. Yue had acquired a boundary around a possible account, not the account itself. That felt like a poor souvenir until she remembered how many other people's memories she had once carried home as though possession were the same thing as understanding.

expansion_song_mei_rest_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_rest_001.text: Yue asked whether there would be a posted starting time at the public entrance. Song said the merchant's household would hang it before evening, once the supper preparations were confirmed. She could name the expected hour but would not promise a finished meal she had no part in cooking. Yue said she would check the notice if her work allowed. The answer gave neither of them a new obligation to arrange the other's night.

expansion_song_mei_rest_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_rest_002.text: The driver began another request for a verse. Song raised her spoon. He held up his bowl in surrender, and their little exchange made Yue laugh more freely than the earlier joke had. She had spent months fearing that every pause in training revealed some failure of discipline. Here a person could leave a skill unused while eating. Rest did not need to demonstrate an eventual benefit before it was allowed to occupy a few minutes.

expansion_song_mei_rest_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_rest_003.text: Yue learned no more about the singer's remembered routes. She kept her notebook closed and drank the last of her water slowly. When Song reached for her bread, the drum stayed silent at her feet. Its presence made the table feel capable of music without requiring any. Yue would still have to ask ordinary questions at the cistern, and she would have no song to make them sound wiser. She found herself willing to arrive that way.

expansion_song_mei_choice.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_choice.text: Song set her palm over the drumhead. Yue had a short interval before Tuo's cistern visit. Which part of the conversation should she pursue?

choices.text: Compare a song's timing with a journey's duration without treating rhythm as a route measure.
Ask how Song distinguishes her own recollection from a line inherited from another singer.
Let the performer finish lunch and ask only when the public supper performance will begin.

expansion_song_mei_common_001.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_common_001.text: A woman at the next table answered the driver's compensation question by tapping her drum twice. 'The sky employs no clerk,' she said. 'A convenient arrangement for the sky.' Her voice had a practiced reach that made the joke audible without making it a performance everyone had purchased. She introduced herself as Song Mei. The mulberry cloth around her shoulders had been mended in a brighter thread, and the drumhead carried a patch close to its rim.

expansion_song_mei_common_002.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_common_002.text: Song had been paid to perform at a merchant's supper that evening. Lunch was her own, as was the brief joke. When the driver asked for the rest of the song, she said he could hear it from the public side of the supper court if he did not mind the smell of food he had not bought. He laughed and returned to his beans. Yue liked that Song could refuse a request without explaining how hard performers worked. The boundary arrived as part of the conversation, not a petition for sympathy.

expansion_song_mei_common_003.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_common_003.text: Song asked whether Yue's west kiln story had happened to her or come down through other workers. Yue said she had been there for some damp-firewood arguments, though she had compressed several into one memory. The performer nodded. Compression was how an evening song stayed an evening song. It could also make one person's complaint sound like the opinion of a whole room. Yue glanced toward the cook, who was busy gathering bowls and had not offered to become a character in anyone's account.

expansion_song_mei_common_004.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_common_004.text: The patched drum made a softer note near its rim. Song said she had once changed the beat in a travel song to give an old singer time to breathe. Later listeners called the extra pause a sign that the route contained another day's march. Yue asked whether she had corrected them. Several times, Song said. The shorter claim had traveled farther. People could remember a tune and still misunderstand why part of it existed.

expansion_song_mei_common_005.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_common_005.text: A man at the far end of the table asked whether the song named a usable well. Song said it named a remembered stop in someone else's account, not the current condition of a water source. She would not sell him a route by singing a place name. He looked irritated, then interested, as if a refusal to provide a map might be a more valuable map in disguise. Yue recognized the move. A limit could become another kind of mystery if the listener was determined to extract a promise.

expansion_song_mei_common_006.speaker: narrator
expansion_song_mei_common_006.text: The meal was nearly over. Song needed to rest her voice before the paid supper, and Tuo would soon take Yue to the cistern. There was time to hear one explanation, compare one remembered detail, or leave the performer to finish her food. Yue could not treat the coming water lesson as permission to interrogate a singer about every well she had named. The desert was larger than the yard. A song's reach did not make its maker responsible for guiding everyone across it.
